name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index 103.8 on 20 Nov, near a 52-week high and up 4.9% over three months, at the Watch line
state: The DXY dollar index stood near 103.8 early on 20 Nov, just below its 52-week high of 103.9 and up 4.9% over three months, at the 5% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). Expectations of a December Fed rate rise have supported the dollar (Kitco, 19 Nov). The level is well inside the 90–108 range and SOFR stayed within 3bp of the Fed's reserve rate (FRED), so no funding strain is visible.
for_you: A strong dollar raises costs for countries and firms that borrow or import in dollars. UK travellers to the US and importers paying in dollars face less favourable exchange rates.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 4.89% has not yet cleared the 4.5% exit line, so Watch holds

sources.title: Kitco — Gold falls below $3,650, silver tumbles as Fed rate concerns pressure metals

why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
